title: Fill in the Blank: External Data
prompt: Test your knowledge of memory sections (.data, .bss, .text), ASCII string literals, pointers, and handling command-line arguments in assembly.

blanks.prompt: Allocate 40 bytes of uninitialized space in the .bss section for a 10-element integer array.
blanks.explanation: Uninitialized space can be allocated in the .bss section with the .skip pseudo-op.
blanks.hint: You want to 'jump over' this amount of memory.

blanks.prompt: Declare a 64-bit integer initialized to 0 in the .data section.
blanks.explanation: A doubleword (.dword) allocates 64 bits (8 bytes) in the data section.
blanks.hint: A word is 32 bits, so you need a 'double' word.

blanks.prompt: Print register w19's contents as a character in GDB.
blanks.explanation: In gdb, use p/c $w19 to print register contents as a character.
blanks.hint: The format specifier is the first letter of 'character'.

blanks.prompt: Make a variable label accessible to other compilation units (files).
blanks.explanation: Use .global if the variable is to be made available to other compilation units.
blanks.hint: It broadens the scope of the variable to the entire program.

blanks.prompt: Declare a null-terminated string literal in the .text section.
blanks.explanation: The .string pseudo-op creates a read-only array of characters that is implicitly null-terminated.
blanks.hint: It is more convenient than using .ascii and adding a 0 manually.
